interactions.title: Nahto and Skoda have been kidnapped
lines: DM: Just in the past few days these attacks have escalated to raids on the near shore of the Vermillion Isles, and two Kenku named Nahto and Skoda—partners, explorers, travelers, wise in the way of the islands, but growing old in years, and not as quick on the wing as they once were—were kidnapped while only, ah, less than a mile off the coast, in a small boat.

before: DM: And music.

DM: Okay. So we are starting our adventure today in the Vermillion Isles, a small archipelago of red rocky cliffs that rise from the warm blue ocean among the vast and ever-changing islands that stretch for thousands of miles between the Green Sea and the Endless Ocean to the east. The Vermillion Isles in the town called Wahacha, where you are.

DM: They're mostly inhabited by Kenku, a flying race of bird folk in Taelgar. Here they make their homes on the towering red cliffs that rise from the sea and dot the dry, scrubby uh interior of the islands; and while the Kenku of the Vermillion Isles are nominally welcoming of outsiders, they do little to make their homes and villages accessible to those without wings, and most of the grounders, as they call the flightless people, humans mostly, but some halflings and others—uh, the grounders mostly live in a few small clusters of buildings around the main harbor.

DM: The five of you have all found your way, and through various routes, some more circuitous than others to the Dolphin’s Rest, a boisterous inn, um, serving the sailors on shore leave from the merchant vessels that ply the trade routes to and around the Vermillion Isles.

DM: Here, in a quiet back room, you've gathered to discuss the problem of raiders, for the past month or so has not been a peaceful time for the Vermillion Isles. Three times now merchant ships on their way to or from Wahacha, have been attacked by raiders of a most unusual nature. They approach in small, swift galleys, feigning distress, while the crew calls for aid, a party slips underwater, seemingly able to breathe comfortably, boring a hole near the waterline of the merchant vessel, and sneaking aboard. Although they have sometimes taken treasure they have generally not focused on treasure or cargo, instead kidnapping people, escaping in the commotion, while the crews of the ship struggle to repair the gaping holes in the hull as water pours in.
